feed.title: DevCentr News
feed.subtitle: News and engineering blog posts from Dev-Centr.

entry.title: When unrelated installers still queue
entry.summary: Open-source Windows installer tooling is mature at copying files and stale everywhere else. The global MSI lock is coarse on purpose — and that is a design gap worth naming.

entry.title: Lightweight agent harness direction
entry.summary: DevCentr is building a T3code-weight local agent runtime on dlang-supplemental infrastructure — harness-neutral rules, ecosystem specialization, token provenance as first UX contract.

entry.title: Agent rules without the harness baked in
entry.summary: Forkable agent-rules templates should not assume Cursor—or any single AI harness. Machine facts belong in HARNESS.md and MEMORIES.md; illustrated architecture now on docs.devcentr.org.

entry.title: After Skia: where rendering is headed
entry.summary: Electron wins the ecosystem until the document grows. Then the renderer—not the feature list—decides whether your app survives two gigabytes of chat. What comes after Skia on Windows and Linux.

entry.title: When the binary assumes one kernel
entry.summary: Almost every compiled program encodes one OS and one CPU. That is a local accident, and the download page is the scar.

entry.title: Unified binary distribution under investigation
entry.summary: Dev-Centr is prototyping a single-download pack of native OS/arch slices, with Binary Tailor stripping foreign headers on delivery.

entry.title: Config files get a Control Panel
entry.summary: UniConfig Config Panel opens other people's INI, YAML, TOML, SDLang, and tfvars with schema-backed settings widgets — including fields the file never mentioned.

entry.title: Intents, not shell translation
entry.summary: One playbook should name what you want. PlayTime binds how on this computer. Equivalence Engine is a catalog -- not a blender that turns bash into PowerShell.

entry.title: When a Cloud project pretends to be an app
entry.summary: Google Cloud forces personal OAuth into Project-shaped boxes—consent, quotas, and API enablement included. Here is the mental model we document instead.

entry.title: When API keys wear token costumes
entry.summary: Vendors keep labeling long-lived dashboard secrets as tokens. Here is the architectural split Dev-Centr is forcing into docs and Secrets Manager—and why the wrong word keeps breaking security reviews.

entry.title: Business Bootstrap becomes a support-systems hub
entry.summary: Founder ops docs grow past email—scheduling, design, and vaults get their own capability areas on docs.devcentr.org.

entry.title: MSI tables land in the generator
entry.summary: msi-generator v0.2 writes real OLE2 compound files, cabinets, and core Windows Installer tables — still unsigned, no longer an empty stub.

entry.title: Easy Installer becomes Ibex
entry.summary: Install Builder EXtension — new name, logo, and OS package registries for the installer-authoring CLI.

entry.title: Easy Installer ships
entry.summary: A CLI and Explorer menu for installer projects and Install in-place PATH — without waiting on a full MSI every time you want a tool on PATH.

entry.title: Easy Installer emits CI pipelines
entry.summary: Scaffold GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Jenkins, CircleCI, or Bitbucket workflows for installer builds — without packaging on your laptop.

entry.title: We’re partnering with OpenShellOrg (on purpose)
entry.summary: DevCentr and OpenShellOrg are locking in the sibling story—toolchain ownership on our side, shell entrypoint honesty on theirs.

entry.title: We’re opening a News desk
entry.summary: Why DevCentr is starting a public News feed—and what you won't find here.

entry.title: Stop dumping people into the docs
entry.summary: We built a Help hub so “I need assistance” doesn't mean “go read the manual.”

entry.title: Our logo shouldn’t need a proprietary player
entry.summary: Why DevCentr's new mark stays in SVG—and why we're cautious about Rive as a default for open brands.
